---
title: "Tables from raw data"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

Most report tables start as a raw data frame: one row per case, test or
event. phwstyle's table builders do the grouping, totals and
percentages for you, and return a data frame that remembers its layout. You
then render that one object with whichever table package suits the output:

| Output | Function |
|---|---|
| Word, PDF, PowerPoint | `phw_flextable()` |
| HTML, Quarto | `phw_gt()` |
| Interactive HTML, Shiny | `phw_reactable()` |
| Excel | `phw_write_xlsx()` |

```{r}
library(phwstyle)
library(dplyr)
set.seed(1)
dat <- tibble(
  group = sample(c("Group A", "Group B", "Group C"), 400, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.45, 0.4, 0.15)),
  type = factor(sample(c("Type 1", "Type 2", "Type 3"), 400, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.45, 0.45, 0.1)),
                levels = c("Type 1", "Type 2", "Type 3")),
  year = sample(2024:2025, 400, replace = TRUE),
  quarter = sample(paste0("Q", 1:4), 400, replace = TRUE),
  days = rpois(400, 3)
)
col_labels <- list(group = "Group", type = "Type", year = "Year", quarter = "Quarter")
```

## Nested groups: `phw_group_table()`

Give the row groups outermost first. Each group row (Group A, B, C)
shows the total for its group, the groups inside are indented, and the main
groups are shaded and separated with space.

```{r}
tab <- phw_group_table(dat, rows = c(group, type), cols = year, labels = col_labels)
phw_flextable(tab, caption = "Counts by group and type", source = "Example data")
```

### Totals

`totals` takes any of `"group"` (totals on each group row), `"subgroup"` (a
block with each type summed across all groups) and `"table"` (a grand
total). `total_position` puts the table total at the top or bottom, and
`subtotal_position = "below"` moves group totals to their own row.

```{r}
phw_group_table(dat, c(group, type), labels = col_labels,
                totals = c("group", "subgroup", "table"),
                subtotal_position = "below", total_position = "top") |>
  phw_flextable()
```

### Layout and percentages

`layout = "columns"` gives each level its own column, so the inner groups
shift to the right. `percent = "parent"` shows each row as a share of the
group above it; `"column"` and `"row"` are also available.

```{r}
phw_group_table(dat, c(group, type), labels = col_labels, layout = "columns",
                percent = "parent", separate = "both") |>
  phw_flextable()
```

### Nested columns

Columns can nest too, here quarters within years, with a total for each
year and overall.

```{r}
nested <- phw_group_table(dat, c(group, type), c(year, quarter), labels = col_labels,
                          col_totals = c("group", "table"))
phw_gt(nested, caption = "Counts by quarter")
```

### Other statistics

By default rows are counted. Give `value` and `fun` for anything else; group
and total rows are calculated from their records, not by adding up rows.

```{r}
phw_group_table(dat, c(group, type), year, value = days,
                fun = function(x) round(mean(x), 1), labels = col_labels) |>
  phw_flextable(caption = "Mean days")
```

### Interactive

```{r}
phw_reactable(nested, caption = "Counts by quarter")
```

## Summary and epidemiology tables

```{r}
cases <- tibble(
  age_group = sample(c("0-14", "15-44", "45-64", "65+"), 300, replace = TRUE),
  sex = sample(c("Female", "Male"), 300, replace = TRUE),
  setting = sample(c("Setting 1", "Setting 2", "Setting 3"), 300, replace = TRUE),
  days = rpois(300, 4),
  outcome = sample(c("Outcome X", "Outcome Y"), 300, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.8, 0.2))
)
```

`phw_summary_table()` gives the "Table 1" of a report: n (%) for
categories and median (IQR) for numbers, split by a group.

```{r}
phw_summary_table(cases, by = outcome,
                  labels = list(age_group = "Age group", sex = "Sex", setting = "Setting",
                                days = "Days to recovery")) |>
  phw_flextable(caption = "Characteristics by outcome")
```

For a table you built yourself, a dplyr summary say, every row looks the
same to the renderers. `phw_as_summary()` marks it as a summary table, and then the bold variable
rows, indented levels and total rows appear in `phw_flextable()`,
`phw_gt()`, `phw_reactable()`, `phw_datatable()` and `phw_write_xlsx()`.
Name the column that says what each row is with `row_type`. Its values are
`"variable"`, `"level"`, `"subtotal"`, `"group"` and `"total"`.

```{r}
by_age <- cases |> count(age_group, name = "cases")
mine <- tibble(
  label = c("Age group", by_age$age_group, "All ages"),
  cases = c(NA, by_age$cases, sum(by_age$cases)),
  kind = c("variable", rep("level", nrow(by_age)), "total")
) |>
  phw_as_summary(row_type = kind, note = "Example data.")
phw_flextable(mine, caption = "Cases by age group")
```

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("DT", quietly = TRUE)}
phw_datatable(mine)
```

`phw_crosstab()` cross-tabulates two variables with totals and optional
percentages, and `phw_flextable_heat()` colours the counts.

```{r}
phw_crosstab(cases, setting, age_group) |>
  phw_flextable() |>
  phw_flextable_heat(j = 2:5)
```

`phw_rate_table()` gives rates with exact Poisson confidence intervals for
several breakdowns at once, from aggregated counts and populations.

```{r}
agg <- tidyr::expand_grid(sex = c("Female", "Male"), age_group = c("0-14", "15-44", "45-64", "65+")) |>
  mutate(cases = rpois(n(), c(10, 25, 35, 50)),
         population = round(runif(n(), 60, 140)) * 1000)
phw_rate_table(agg, c(age_group, sex), cases, population,
               labels = list(age_group = "Age group", sex = "Sex")) |>
  phw_flextable()
```

`phw_risk_table()` gives attack rates and relative risks by exposure.

```{r}
ob <- tibble(exposure_a = sample(c("Yes", "No"), 120, replace = TRUE),
             exposure_b = sample(c("Yes", "No"), 120, replace = TRUE)) |>
  mutate(ill = rbinom(n(), 1, if_else(exposure_a == "Yes", 0.6, 0.15)))
phw_risk_table(ob, c(exposure_a, exposure_b), ill, labels = list(exposure_a = "Exposure A", exposure_b = "Exposure B")) |>
  phw_flextable()
```

## gtsummary

`use_phw_gtsummary()` sets a theme, so every gtsummary table is styled when
printed with gt or converted with `as_flex_table()`.

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("gtsummary", quietly = TRUE)}
use_phw_gtsummary()
cases |>
  select(age_group, sex, days, outcome) |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(by = outcome)
```

```{r, include = FALSE, eval = requireNamespace("gtsummary", quietly = TRUE)}
gtsummary::reset_gtsummary_theme()
```
